runs.market_commentary:
Asian markets closed the week strongly with the Nikkei 225 posting a 1.26% gain on Friday, closing at 65,021 — its highest level in over a month — driven by easing rate-hike concerns from the Bank of Japan and continued enthusiasm around Japanese semiconductor and robotics exporters benefiting from South Korea's semiconductor export boom (exports tripled year-over-year). Broader Asia sentiment was supported by a pickup in global trade volumes, which rose 8.8% YoY and 3.3% month-over-month in June, the second-fastest monthly gain since 2023.

European markets closed modestly higher on Friday, with the DAX at 21,847 (+0.38%) and FTSE at 8,718 (+0.22%), though gains were capped by a troubling inflation reading: Euro zone CPI climbed back above 3%, prompting renewed speculation about additional ECB rate action. The AI data center construction boom was flagged by Bloomberg as insufficient to offset a broader US and European construction sector slump, pressuring rate-sensitive real estate and utilities stocks.

US markets are closed Monday September 7 for Labor Day, making this a four-day trading week. Last Friday saw mixed pre-market futures — Dow futures slipped ~10 pts (-0.02%), S&P 500 futures -0.06%, and Nasdaq-100 futures -0.10% — but sentiment firmed intraday following Trump comments that 'market will go up,' per Benzinga. The key macro focus for the week is the August inflation print: PPI drops Thursday before the bell and CPI drops Friday before the bell. Any CPI surprise above 3% would reprice Fed rate-cut odds materially. Kroger reports fiscal Q2 earnings Friday as well, providing a consumer health read.

ideas.catalyst: Morgan Stanley maintains NVDA as its core AI play heading into a week where AI data center demand commentary is expected from multiple tech conferences.
ideas.thesis: NVIDIA's data center GPU franchise continues to benefit from hyperscaler capex acceleration, with South Korea semiconductor export data (tripled YoY) confirming robust end-demand across the supply chain. The stock has institutional tailwinds entering the holiday-shortened week with no adverse earnings risk until late Q3.
ideas.key_risk: Any CPI upside surprise Friday could reprice risk assets broadly, pressuring high-multiple tech names including NVDA.

ideas.catalyst: Macquarie raised Snowflake's price target from $200 to $350 this week, maintaining Neutral — a massive $150 PT jump signals significantly improved fundamental view on the data cloud platform.
ideas.thesis: The sharp Macquarie PT increase to $350 suggests Snowflake's AI-native data platform is gaining enterprise traction faster than consensus expects, likely driven by its Cortex AI workloads. With the stock trading well below the new target, the setup favors upside into the next earnings cycle.
ideas.key_risk: Rising rates from a hot CPI print would hurt growth multiples; Snowflake carries a premium valuation that compresses in risk-off environments.

ideas.catalyst: FDA PDUFA date for zidesamtinib (ROS1+ non-small cell lung cancer) is September 18, 2026 — 12 days away.
ideas.thesis: Zidesamtinib targets a validated oncology niche with significant unmet need; ROS1+ NSCLC patients have limited approved options and ROS1 inhibitors have shown strong clinical profiles in this indication. A positive FDA decision on Sept 18 would be a transformative binary catalyst for this small-cap biotech.
ideas.key_risk: Binary FDA risk — a Complete Response Letter or label restriction would send the stock sharply lower; position sizing accordingly.

sources.label: Biotech Stocks Facing FDA Decision Sept 2026 - RTTNews

ideas.catalyst: Apitegromab has a FDA PDUFA date of September 30, 2026 for the treatment of spinal muscular atrophy (SMA).
ideas.thesis: SMA is a high-value rare disease market; apitegromab targets a mechanism complementary to existing SMA treatments (Spinraza, Zolgensma) and could carve out significant market share if approved. Scholar Rock's recent 8-K filings suggest the company is positioning for a commercial launch.
ideas.key_risk: FDA may request additional data given the complexity of SMA combination therapy; approval is not guaranteed and timeline could slip to 2027.

ideas.catalyst: Goldman Sachs maintains UPS as a top pick with a $132 price target implying ~29% upside; stock yields 6.39%, one of the highest in Goldman's coverage universe.
ideas.thesis: Global trade volumes surged 8.8% YoY in June, the second-fastest monthly growth since 2023, directly benefiting UPS's international and domestic package networks. At a 6.39% dividend yield with Goldman's $132 PT, the risk-reward skews favorably for income-oriented investors.
ideas.key_risk: Any deterioration in consumer spending or a trade-war escalation could dampen package volume growth and pressure the dividend if cash flows weaken.

sources.label: Goldman Sachs Top Picks September 2026 - 24/7 Wall St.
Kiplinger Economic Data Week of Sept 7-11

ideas.catalyst: Morgan Stanley names Amazon as a top pick alongside NVDA for the AI infrastructure supercycle, with AWS continuing to take cloud market share.
ideas.thesis: Amazon's tripartite exposure to AI (AWS Bedrock, custom Trainium chips, Alexa+) creates compounding optionality across cloud, consumer AI, and advertising. AWS re-acceleration is the key near-term driver and management commentary at upcoming conferences should serve as a positive catalyst.
ideas.key_risk: Antitrust scrutiny remains a tail risk; any regulatory action against AWS or the retail marketplace could overhang the stock.

sources.label: Morgan Stanley Top Picks - TheStreet Pro
Goldman Sachs & Morgan Stanley Picks Sept 2026 - CNBC

ideas.catalyst: Macquarie raised Zscaler's price target from $172 to $200, maintaining Outperform, reflecting confidence in the zero-trust security platform's enterprise penetration.
ideas.thesis: Zero-trust architecture continues to be a board-level priority across enterprises as hybrid work and AI tool proliferation expand attack surfaces. Zscaler's platform-based approach is outpacing point-product competitors, and the Macquarie PT lift suggests improving visibility into the next few quarters.
ideas.key_risk: Cybersecurity spending can be discretionary; any macro slowdown signaled by this week's CPI print could cause CIOs to delay purchasing decisions.

ideas.catalyst: Wells Fargo raised Amgen's price target from $400 to $435, maintaining Equal-Weight — a constructive PT lift suggesting improved pipeline or revenue visibility.
ideas.thesis: Amgen's obesity pipeline (MariTide) and inflammation franchise (Repatha, Otezla) provide durable growth drivers while the stock's relative defensive characteristics offer portfolio ballast heading into a potential CPI shock this Friday. The $435 Wells Fargo PT implies meaningful upside from current levels.
ideas.key_risk: Pipeline setbacks in obesity (any MariTide trial data miss) or biosimilar competition to legacy products could weigh on the stock.

ideas.catalyst: UBS raised Teva's price target to $48 with a Buy rating, reflecting improved confidence in the generic pharma giant's debt reduction and pipeline progression.
ideas.thesis: Teva is executing on a multi-year turnaround anchored by opioid settlement resolution, biosimilar launches, and the growing AUSTEDO franchise for tardive dyskinesia and Huntington's chorea. At UBS's $48 target, Teva trades at a significant discount to specialty pharma peers, offering a valuation re-rating opportunity.
ideas.key_risk: Teva carries significant debt; rising interest rates from a hot inflation print could pressure refinancing economics and delay deleveraging targets.

ideas.catalyst: Kroger reports fiscal Q2 2026 earnings Friday September 11, with consensus expecting EPS of $1.06 on revenue of $34.61 billion — a potential beat given grocery inflation dynamics.
ideas.thesis: Food-at-home inflation has stayed sticky above general CPI, benefiting Kroger's private label and loyalty program economics. If Thursday's PPI and Friday's CPI show continued services inflation, Kroger's grocery pricing power narrative strengthens as consumers trade down from restaurants.
ideas.key_risk: Post-merger integration costs (from the Albertsons saga) and competitive pressure from Walmart and Amazon Fresh could disappoint on margins versus the EPS consensus.

deals.headline: Eli Lilly Acquires Merida Biosciences for Autoimmune Pipeline
deals.description: Eli Lilly announced an agreement to acquire Merida Biosciences, a privately-held biotech developing a new class of precision therapeutics for serious autoimmune and allergic diseases, on September 1, 2026. The deal underscores Lilly's strategy to diversify beyond its blockbuster GLP-1 weight-loss franchise into high-value immunology.
deals.impact: Bullish for LLY – adds pipeline optionality in a fast-growing immune-mediated disease market without dilutive equity issuance.

deals.headline: EQT Pays $2B for Majority Stake in McGill and Partners
deals.description: EQT, the Swedish private equity giant, announced plans on September 4, 2026 to pay $2 billion for a majority stake in McGill and Partners, a specialty (re)insurance broker. The deal reflects continued PE appetite for fee-generating insurance distribution assets, which carry lower catastrophe risk than underwriters.
deals.impact: Moderately bullish for EQT shares as the deal signals disciplined capital deployment into high-quality insurance distribution at a time of robust commercial lines pricing.

deals.headline: SHEIN Lists on Hong Kong Stock Exchange in Landmark Fast-Fashion IPO
deals.description: SHEIN completed its listing on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange on September 1, 2026, in one of the year's most anticipated retail IPOs. The Chinese-founded fast-fashion giant had faced multiple delays and regulatory hurdles across US and UK listing attempts before pivoting to Hong Kong.
deals.impact: Competitive pressure signal for Western fast-fashion and e-commerce players; capital markets constructive on Hong Kong bourse's ability to attract major listings.

deals.headline: FDA Grants Accelerated Approval for TUDRIQEV in Advanced Melanoma
deals.description: On August 6, 2026, the FDA granted accelerated approval for TUDRIQEV (vusolimogene oderparepvec-wtpg) for adult patients with unresectable advanced cutaneous melanoma who experienced disease progression on an anti-PD-1 antibody. The approval opens a new commercial opportunity in the competitive checkpoint inhibitor-refractory melanoma market.
deals.impact: Positive regulatory precedent for oncolytic virotherapy; bullish signal for other companies in the immuno-oncology and oncolytic virus space ahead of September FDA calendar.

deals.headline: Anthropic IPO Expected Late September / October 2026
deals.description: Bloomberg reported on August 24, 2026, that Anthropic, the AI safety company and maker of Claude, is anticipated to pursue an IPO in late September or October 2026. Separately, OURA Health (the smart ring maker) may also IPO as early as September, per the same report.
deals.impact: Potential landmark AI IPO would be a sentiment catalyst for AI infrastructure and software names; could siphon capital from listed AI proxies like NVDA, MSFT, GOOGL if institutional reallocation occurs.

key_events.headline: Labor Day — US Markets Closed Monday September 7
key_events.impact: Shortened 4-day trading week; lower liquidity Monday could amplify moves when markets reopen Tuesday.

key_events.headline: PPI Report (August) — Thursday September 10
key_events.impact: Producer price inflation is the leading indicator for CPI; a hot print above +0.3% MoM would pressure Treasuries and rate-sensitive equities.

key_events.headline: CPI Report (August) — Friday September 11
key_events.impact: The week's defining data point; consensus expects ~2.8% YoY. Any print above 3% would materially reprice Fed rate-cut expectations for 2026.

key_events.headline: Euro Zone Inflation Returns Above 3%, ECB Rate Action Eyed
key_events.impact: Higher ECB terminal rate expectations pressure European bond markets and reduce equity multiple expansion for European stocks.

key_events.headline: South Korea Semiconductor Exports Triple Year-Over-Year
key_events.impact: Strong validation of AI chip demand cycle; bullish for memory and logic semiconductor names globally (Samsung, SK Hynix, TSMC, NVDA, AMD).

key_events.headline: Kroger Fiscal Q2 2026 Earnings — Friday September 11
key_events.impact: Consensus: EPS $1.06 on revenue $34.61B. A beat would confirm grocery pricing power; a miss on margins would weigh on consumer staples broadly.

risk_calendar.desc: Labor Day — US equity and bond markets closed. Expect thin global liquidity.
Producer Price Index (PPI) for August — released before market open. Consensus ~+0.2% MoM.
Consumer Price Index (CPI) for August — released before market open. Consensus ~2.8% YoY. Key Fed pivot signal.
Kroger (KR) fiscal Q2 2026 earnings. Consensus EPS $1.06 on $34.61B revenue.
Zidesamtinib (NUVL) — FDA decision for ROS1+ non-small cell lung cancer. Binary biotech catalyst.
Apitegromab (SRRK) for spinal muscular atrophy and OST-HER2 (OSTX) BLA review — dual binary biotech events.

runs.market_commentary: Asian equity markets closed mostly higher Friday, with the Nikkei 225 advancing 1.26% to 65,021.
US markets surged on the August jobs blowout.
Asian markets sold off sharply overnight.
Asian markets closed mostly lower Tuesday.
